html:
The Land Apportionment Act of 1930 divided the land of Southern Rhodesia by race, giving about half of it, including most of the best farmland, to a small white minority and pushing Africans into reserves.

Africans could not buy land in white areas, and many were moved off land they had farmed. The reserves became crowded and overgrazed, and young men had to seek work on white farms, mines and towns.

The act and laws that followed shaped the economy and politics of Rhodesia for fifty years. Land was a main cause of the Bush War, and the unequal holdings left by it led to the fast-track land reform after 2000 in Zimbabwe.
sum: The Land Apportionment Act of 1930 divided the land of Southern Rhodesia by race, giving about half of it, including most of the best farmland, to a small white minority and pushing Africans into reserves.
